title: A method for quantifying phonotaxis in the concave-eared torrent frog
protocol: Catch females of O. tormota at night.
Keep individual females in an open-top plastic container with a gauze cover.
Use an ultrasonic microphone and PC Tape system to record calls.
Use a digital audio recorder with a microphone to record calls.
Save call records as wave files.
Analyze and display call records using the SELENA software.
Determine which calls are produced by males or females.
Select a recorded female call for storage on the flash memory of a Play unit.
Store the selected call on an MP3 player for field tests if needed.
Broadcast the female call through a Play unit with audible and ultrasonic loudspeakers.
Position the playback device 1 m away from a frog in the field or on an indoor arena.
Adjust the broadcast level to ~80-90 dB SPL.
Digitally filter the call with low-pass, high-pass filters at a cutoff frequency of 20 kHz.
Apply a slope of 100 dB per octave for filtering.
Broadcast filtered calls through audible and/or ultrasonic loudspeakers.
Carry out acoustic playback experiments at night in field or in a quiet and darkened indoor room, approximately 1 km from the frog's natural habitat.
Present playback stimuli at a rate of 1 call every 15 seconds over a 5-minute period.
Place an isolated male frog on an indoor arena (3.5 x 4.5 m) under a removable glass cover (inside diameter: 8.5 cm), 1 meter in front of the loudspeaker.
Use the PC Tape system or a digital audio recorder with a microphone mounted on a tripod and placed 10 cm from the loudspeaker to record frog's vocalizations and stimuli.
Record males' phonotactic movements and vocalizations using an infrared videorecorder under infrared illumination.
Playback the videotaped record of the experiment.
Extract audio signals from video files using software (e.g., Cool Edit Pro 2.0).
Depict scaled tracings of each male frog from videotaped records.
Measure the frog hop distance in cm.

Calculate the azimuthal angle using the formula alpha = arcsin(d/D), where d is the vertical length from the hop landing site to the line between the hop start site and the center of loudspeaker, and D is the hop distance.
Calculate the index of straightness for males' phonotactic movements.
